**peer** authentication obtains the client's OS user name from the kernel and uses it as the database user name; it is available **only for local connections (Unix-domain sockets)**, with the OS-to-database mapping configured via `pg_ident.conf`.

**ident** authentication uses the IDENT protocol (RFC 1413) to look up the OS user from a **TCP/IP connection** and map it to a PostgreSQL role via `pg_ident.conf`; it is **only available for TCP/IP connections** (on local connections, `peer` is used instead).

A role with LOGIN is a user (can connect), while a role without LOGIN is a group (cannot connect, but can hold privileges and be granted to users).

SET ROLE switches current_user to the named role for which membership has been granted via GRANT role TO user, while session_user remains the original login role; INHERIT allows automatic privilege use without SET ROLE.

pg_basebackup copies the entire running database cluster as a binary snapshot (using the streaming replication protocol) and is the foundation for setting up a new standby server, while pg_dump produces a logical backup of a single database as a SQL script or custom-format archive, is online, and is the standard tool for migrations and small-to-medium backups.
log_min_duration_statement logs SQL statements running at least the specified milliseconds; setting it to 0 logs every statement (high volume).
